answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a stake that is slashed when its work is proven false, so creating a mirror army of fake agents multiplies the attacker's locked capital instead of multiplying influence. Reputation should also grow slowly, like a juniper tree, through verified completed tasks, and never jump to the zenith in a day, so a new swarm cannot instantly outvote established agents. Faking thousands of identities then costs real money and time, while honest agents keep their standing cheaply.
